name: Ramp
verdict: Ramp's Partner Integration process requires approval before production access: it reviews your flows and asks for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI or a recent pen test. No review times documented; likely several weeks.
needGuide: Yes — request sandbox access, then apply for production access with your security documents ready.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 with client credentials for internal server-to-server use (token about 10 days, no refresh token) and authorization code for third-party apps acting for other businesses (access token default 1 hour; code valid 10 minutes; refresh grant must be enabled; HTTPS redirect URIs; state recommended). Token endpoint POST /developer/v1/token with Basic auth. A refresh returns a new access token but not a new refresh token and does not extend the refresh token's expiry.

effort.timeToFirstTest: 30–60 min in sandbox after getting sandbox access
effort.timeToProduction: unknown (no review times documented); likely several weeks

approval.gate: Partner Integration process: Build, then Apply for Production Access (Ramp reviews your integration flows; 'approval is required before production access'), then Beta Testing, then optional Public Listing on the Ramp Integrations page. Expect to supply SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI or a recent third-party pen test (full report), a public security policy URL, a monitored security contact and written data-handling descriptions; early-stage companies may substitute a recent pen test. The cards:read_vault scope needs extra security review. A Technology Partnerships Application exists.

scopes.why: resource:permission scopes; start read-only. cards:read_vault needs an extra security review.
scopes.summary: resource:permission pattern (transactions:read, bills:read, cards:read, users:read, business:read); start read-only and add write scopes as needed. cards:read_vault requires additional security review.

cost: Free; Ramp takes no fee and partners bill customers directly
prerequisites: Account and owner: A developer with access to the Ramp Developer Console in your own Ramp account (likely an Admin); a partnerships owner for the application; Security and Legal for the attestations.

Where you register: Ramp Developer Console (reached from the Ramp dashboard; exact menu path not in the docs read) → create app → client ID and secret → enable Authorization Code and Refresh Token grants → add redirect URIs. Sandbox and production each need their own app.
Cost: Free; Ramp takes no fee and partners bill customers directly

registerAt.path: Ramp Developer Console (reached from the Ramp dashboard; exact menu path not in the docs read) → create app → client ID and secret → enable Authorization Code and Refresh Token grants → add redirect URIs. Sandbox and production each need their own app.

steps.do: Request sandbox access and create a sandbox app in the Developer Console
Enable Authorization Code and Refresh Token grants; register HTTPS redirect URIs
Implement the flow with read-only scopes first (transactions:read, bills:read, cards:read, users:read, business:read) and store refresh tokens
Handle refresh-token expiry by restarting the authorization flow
Prepare security evidence: SOC 2 or pen test report, security policy URL, security contact, data-handling write-up
Submit the Technology Partnerships Application and Production Access request via a Developer API support ticket
Create a separate production app, then complete Ramp's beta test with a pilot customer admin

roles.team: A developer with access to the Ramp Developer Console in your own Ramp account (likely an Admin); a partnerships owner for the application; Security and Legal for the attestations.
roles.customer: A Ramp Admin or Business Owner (users holding the Developer API authorization permission) must authorize; others see 'Business not authorized to use this application'.

testing: Sandbox at demo.ramp.com (UI) and demo-api.ramp.com (API) with no real money; press Cmd+J for demo actions (mark bills or reimbursements paid, add transactions), which need Admin, Business Owner or AP Clerk roles.
Request sandbox access through Ramp's form; rate limits not documented.

blockers.fix: Apply early with security evidence ready.

blockers.problem: Refreshing does not extend or replace the refresh token, so users must re-authorize when it expires
The Refresh Token grant must be enabled on the app, and sandbox and production need separate apps
Non-admin customer users get 'Business not authorized'
blockers.fix: Ask an Admin or Business Owner to authorize.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth and token handling, run sandbox tests, draft the partnership application, security write-ups and listing assets. Ramp documents a CLI auth flow for agents and a request page for adding redirect URIs to the Ramp MCP.
automation.humanMust: Developer Console login, partner application and agreement, security attestations and reports, a customer Admin or Business Owner authorizing, and any support-ticket back and forth with Ramp.

uncertain: Developer Console menu path and who may create apps, review timelines, partnership application criteria, PKCE support, sandbox rate limits (several Ramp guide pages were empty).
